failure_summary: render_decision.link (L3) supplies an outcome-only frame ("Column 7 makes your opponent work hardest for it; the move you played only speeds up the finish") plus a guardrail forbidding any statement that the played move enabled the pattern, so all 3/3 runs restate the outcome and none names the actual cause the prompt itself carries — the played move lands at c1r3, directly under the opponent's completing square c1r4, which the board confirms flips from non-gravity-top [X] on the decision board to gravity-top <*> after column 1 (solver: col1 -5 / col7 -4 before, +5 for Green immediately after the played move).
notes: A7a fails 3/3 (deterministic): every run explains only that column 7 makes the opponent "work hardest" / that column 1 "speeds up the finish" — outcome, not cause; the decisive fact (column 1 raises the stack to the opponent's completing square c1r4, making the diagonal c4r1-c3r2-c2r3-c1r4 immediately playable) is present in the prompt (Decision block: "Played move: column 1 (lands at c1r3)"; afterPlayed board lists "immediate at c1r4 (opp)") but the L3 guardrail forbids saying the played move enabled it and the frame never supplies the permitted alternative ("column 7 keeps column 1 low"). A4 fails run 1: served text says the opponent's "next-move four in column 1, row 4", but on the decision board (truthBoard for that handle) column 1 has height 2 so c1r4 is NOT gravity-top — the prompt's own reading key explicitly forbids that upgrade; run 1 also calls the diagonal "the four-in-a-row line on column 1" when it spans c1-c4. G1 fails run 1 for the same contradiction with the rendered frame ("not yet reachable — the column needs to fill first"). G7 judgment fails run 0: the single-square handle opp-major (spec c1r4, role "a single square completing your opponent's four-in-a-row line") wraps the words "column 1", a column-shaped phrase lighting one square — the exact shape mismatch the prompt's MATCH THE SHAPE rule forbids; contributing cause is the render's own role text, which leads with "the one in column 1". G7 membership (a/b) passed mechanically on all runs and annotationRepairs is empty on all 3, so no G7c auto-fail. A3 passes: the named tactic (opponent immediate threat at c1r4 on diagonal c4r1-c3r2-c2r3-c1r4) is board-true and is the decisive one. A5 passes 3/3 on servedExplanation: 2nd person, no field names, and the guard humanized run 1/run 2's raw c1r4 to "column 1, row 4" before serving. A5b is N/A (player 2 but boardState is "closing", not "opening"). Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only and null for run 2 (observed run 2 text is consistent with run 0 on all of them). A1/A2/A6 copied verbatim from the mechanical json (all pass, all 3 runs).
